{"id":"mimid-s6a3","title":"stock_rust_client_chats_through_two_daemons times out under the full parallel suite (PATIENCE 15s)","description":"Observed 2026-11-22 during a full `cargo test --workspace --all-features`:

  thread 'stock_rust_client_chats_through_two_daemons' panicked at
  crates/mimid-agent/tests/stock_rust_client.rs:346:
  a StateChange on the reconnecting stream: Elapsed(())
  test result: FAILED ... finished in 19.17s

Run alone, the same test passes in 2.46 seconds. So it is the parallel
load, not the assertion: the full suite builds and runs 210 test
binaries, many of which start servers and open sockets, and the wait at
line 337 is bounded by common/mod.rs's PATIENCE = 15s. A reconnecting
EventSource stream that would deliver in well under a second idle does
not always get there in 15 under that contention.

NOT caused by the push_crypto move in the same session: that change only
relocates RFC 8291 and RFC 8292 code from mimid-agent-irc to
mimid-agent-store with no behaviour change, and nothing in it touches
EventSource, StateChange or the daemon's streams. The test also passed in
a full-suite run earlier the same day, before the move.

WHY IT MATTERS: CI runs the same command, so this will fail there
intermittently, and an intermittent failure in a reconnect test is the
kind that gets re-run until green rather than read.

OPTIONS, cheapest first:
1. Raise PATIENCE, or give this one wait a longer budget than the
   others. Cheap, and honest if the only problem is contention -- but it
   makes a real regression here take longer to notice.
2. Make the test deterministic rather than timed: wait on a signal that
   the reconnect has completed rather than racing a 15s clock. Better,
   more work.
3. Reduce test-binary parallelism for the heavy integration tests, which
   also touches the 25-minute wall clock recorded in bead mimid-gn2v:
   most of that is link time, but the run phase is where this contends.

Note the interaction with mimid-gn2v: if a faster linker shortens the
build, more test binaries run concurrently rather than staggered behind
compilation, which could make this MORE frequent, not less. Worth
re-measuring this test's flake rate after any linker change.","status":"open","priority":3,"issue_type":"task","owner":"mark@reviewcommit.com","created_at":"2026-11-23T06:04:36.482979314Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","updated_at":"2026-11-23T06:04:36.482979314Z"}
